title: Inside the model: tokens, context and attention
hook: How text is cut up, what fits on the desk, and why models trip on codes, counting and long inputs.
inPlainWords: A model does not read letters or words. It reads tokens, which are small pieces of text. It can only look at a limited number of tokens at once, called the context window, and inside that window it uses attention to decide which earlier pieces matter for the next one. This explains many odd mistakes.

useCase.title: Why does the bot fumble codes, counts and long emails?
useCase.story: The assistant misreads the code XR-2040-B, miscounts the letters in a name, loses track of the request inside a very long email chain, and answers differently when the same fact appears at the start or in the middle of a long prompt.

approaches.name: Assume it reads like a person
approaches.what: Treat the model as if it sees words and letters.
approaches.avoidWhen: Codes, exact counts and long inputs.
approaches.example: Ask it to count the letters in a long name.

approaches.name: Send exact jobs to tools
approaches.what: Let code do counting, math and exact matching.
approaches.example: Use a lookup tool for XR-2040-B.

approaches.name: Place key facts clearly
approaches.what: Put instructions and key data in clear sections, and repeat the critical ones.
approaches.example: State the customer's request at the start and again at the end.

approaches.name: Shorten and select the input
approaches.avoidWhen: You cut context the answer needs.
approaches.example: Summarize old messages and keep the last five in full.

approaches.name: Chunk long inputs and combine
approaches.what: Split the input, process each part, then merge.
approaches.avoidWhen: Tasks that need the whole picture at once.
approaches.example: Summarize each part of a 200-message thread, then merge.

approaches.name: Choose a model with a bigger window
approaches.what: Pick a model with more room.
approaches.avoidWhen: As a substitute for tidy input. Cost and accuracy can suffer.
approaches.example: A long-context model for a full contract.

challenge.question: The bot mishandles product codes and a 200-message thread. What is the best fix?

options.text: Use tools for exact lookups, trim and summarize the thread, put key facts up front, and test with long-input cases
options.why: It works with how the model actually reads.

options.text: Tell the model to try harder
options.why: Effort is not the limit. The way it reads is.

options.text: Paste everything and hope the window is big enough
options.why: It may fit, but it is slow, costly and details get lost.

options.text: Retrain the model on product codes
options.why: Expensive, and codes change all the time.

bestCase.title: Give exact jobs to tools and keep the desk tidy
bestCase.example: The code XR-2040-B goes to a lookup tool. Old messages are summarized and the last five stay in full. The request is stated at the start of the prompt. Answers stay consistent and cost less.

worstCase.title: Pasting everything and hoping
worstCase.example: The whole 200-message thread is pasted in. The real request sits in the middle and is ignored, and the model answers an older question. The code is misread as a similar one, and the customer gets the wrong charger.

route.travelling: A 200-message thread ending "Same problem, see XR-2040-B"

steps.label: Long thread arrives
steps.goes: Two hundred messages and a product code.

steps.label: Trim and summarize
steps.goes: Old messages are summarized. The last five stay in full.
steps.goesWrong: The whole thread is pasted in and the key request gets buried.

steps.label: Exact things go to tools
steps.goes: The product code is looked up, not "read".

steps.label: Prompt with key facts first
steps.goes: The request and rules are placed at the start.

steps.label: Model answers
steps.goes: It reads a small, tidy desk.

takeaway: Models read tokens, not words, and only see what fits on the desk. Give exact jobs to tools and keep the desk tidy.
